territorial_scope.description: Applies to campaign communications in Indiana elections, as an amendment to the Indiana Code.

evidence.quote: Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of Indiana

summary.short: Indiana HB 1133 (2024) adds IC 3-9-8 to the Indiana Code. Campaign communications that include fabricated media depicting a candidate must carry a prescribed disclaimer. A depicted candidate may sue the payer, sponsor or knowing disseminator for damages, injunctive relief and fees. Effective upon passage.
summary.long: HB 1133 adds a new chapter, IC 3-9-8, on digitally altered media in elections. A campaign communication is defined as one that advocates for or against a clearly identified candidate, is intended to injure a candidate or influence an election outcome, or solicits a contribution. Fabricated media covers three categories: altered recordings that materially misdepict an individual and are not recognizable as altered, non-consensual lifelike audio or visual imitations used to convey a fictional depiction, and depictions of artificially generated persons that are not recognizable imitations of an identifiable individual. Candidate includes individuals holding elected office at federal, state, school board or local level. If a campaign communication includes fabricated media depicting a candidate, the payer must include a disclaimer stating that elements of the media have been digitally altered or artificially generated, separate from the existing disclaimer under IC 3-9-3-2.5(d). Format rules apply to printed, audio and video communications, including reading in each language used, minimum volume, and repetition at two-minute intervals for audio longer than two minutes. A candidate depicted in fabricated media in a communication lacking the required disclaimer may bring a civil action against the payer, the sponsor, and a disseminator who knowingly, intentionally or recklessly altered or removed the disclaimer. Prevailing plaintiffs may recover actual damages, injunctive relief, and court costs and attorney's fees. The plaintiff must prove by clear and convincing evidence the depiction. Courts must expedite such hearings. Section 2 declares an emergency.}},

notes: Bill text as provided (Indiana HB 1133, 2024). The document gives no passage, signing or effective date beyond '[EFFECTIVE UPON PASSAGE]' on Section 1 and an emergency clause in Section 2. Section 1 adds a new chapter, IC 3-9-8, to the Indiana Code; it does not amend, repeal or implement a named instrument. Internal points: Sec. 1(b)(1)(C) uses 'fabricated media' before Sec. 3 defines it; Sec. 2(a) makes 'candidate' subject to subsection (b), and the document does not say how (b) interacts with IC 3-5-2-6 beyond that. Source formatting has missing spaces (e.g., 'Sec. 2.(a)For purposes of this chapter,subject to subsection(b)'); quotes reproduce the text as printed.
